The 2010 Triple J Hottest 100 was announced and played on January 26, 2011.[1] It is the eighteenth countdown of the most popular songs of the year, as chosen by the listeners of Australian radio station Triple J.

Voting commenced at midnight on Monday 20 December 2010, and closed at midnight on Sunday 16 January 2011. 1.26 million votes were recorded from 152 countries, a new record number of votes.

Records

[edit | edit source]
  • Angus & Julia Stone are the first Australian band to win the Hottest 100 since Augie March in 2006. This is also the first countdown since 1994 which features female vocalist in the winning song. Julia Stone is also the first woman to win the Hottest 100 time since Janet English in 1996.
  • For a second year in a row a Triple J Unearthed artist has cracked the Top 10 (Art vs. Science No. 2 in 2009, Little Red No. 2, Boy & Bear No. 5 and Art vs Science No. 9 in 2010).
  • John Butler Trio scored the No. 39 position for the second year in a row.
  • Both members of Gnarls Barkley got a respective track in the list with different bands; Danger Mouse with Broken Bells and Cee-Lo Green with a solo track.
  • Ian Kenny has now appeared in the Hottest 100 every year since 2005 with both Karnivool and Birds of Tokyo.
  • For the first time since 2005 no artist from France appeared in the Hottest 100.
  • Chiddy Bangs "Opposite of Adults" samples the song "Kids" by MGMT which came fifth in the 2008 countdown.
  • "Runaway" by Kanye West becomes the equal longest song to appear in a countdown, alongside "Jesus of Suburbia" by Green Day which came in at No. 61 in 2005.
  • Robert Smith's collaboration on the Crystal Castles cover of "Not in Love" set the record for the longest absence between countdowns (13 years); Smith last appeared in the 1997 countdown with The Cure.
  • Nicki Minaj is the first artist from Trinidad and Tobago to appear in the Hottest 100.
  • Following Charles Haddon's death in August 2010, Ou Est Le Swimming Pool's two appearances marks the first posthumous appearance of an artist since Jeff Buckley in the 2004 countdown.
  • As of the 2025 Hottest 100, the 2010 countdown is the last Hottest 100 not to feature at least one Like a Version.

Top 20 Albums of 2010

[edit | edit source]

Triple J Listeners voted for their favourite album of 2010 in a similar format to the Hottest 100. Voters were allowed to vote for any album released in 2010 and were limited to ten votes.

Bold indicates the winner of the Hottest 100, while Tame Impala's Innerspeaker won the J Award for Australian Album of the Year.

win the Hottest 100 since [[Augie March]] in [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2006|2006]]. This is also the first countdown since [[Triple J Hottest 100, 1994|1994]] which features female vocalist in the winning song. [[Julia Stone]] is also the first woman to win the Hottest 100 time since Janet English in [[Triple J Hottest 100, 1996|1996]]. * For a second year in a row a Triple J Unearthed artist has cracked the Top 10 ([[Art vs. Science]] No. 2 in [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2009|2009]], [[Little Red (band)|Little Red]] No. 2, [[Boy & Bear]] No. 5 and Art vs Science No. 9 in 2010). * [[John Butler Trio]] scored the No. 39 position for the second year in a row. * Both members of [[Gnarls Barkley]] got a respective track in the list with different bands; [[Danger Mouse (musician)|Danger Mouse]] with [[Broken Bells]] and [[Cee-Lo Green]] with a solo track. * Ian Kenny has now appeared in the Hottest 100 every year since [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2005|2005]] with both [[Karnivool]] and [[Birds of Tokyo]]. * For the first time since [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2005|2005]] no artist from [[France]] appeared in the Hottest 100. * [[Chiddy Bang]]s "[[Opposite of Adults]]" samples the song "[[Kids (MGMT song)|Kids]]" by [[MGMT]] which came fifth in the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2008|2008]] countdown. * "[[Runaway (Kanye West song)|Runaway]]" by [[Kanye West]] becomes the equal longest song to appear in a countdown, alongside "[[Jesus of Suburbia]]" by [[Green Day]] which came in at No. 61 in [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2005|2005]]. * [[Robert Smith (musician)|Robert Smith]]'s collaboration on the [[Crystal Castles]] cover of "[[Not in Love (Platinum Blonde song)#Crystal Castles version|Not in Love]]" set the record for the longest absence between countdowns (13 years); Smith last appeared in the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 1997|1997 countdown]] with [[The Cure]]. * [[Nicki Minaj]] is the first artist from [[Trinidad and Tobago]] to appear in the Hottest 100. * Following Charles Haddon's death in August 2010, [[Ou Est Le Swimming Pool]]'s two appearances marks the first posthumous appearance of an artist since [[Jeff Buckley]] in the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2004|2004 countdown]]. * As of the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2025|2025 Hottest 100]], the 2010 countdown is the last Hottest 100 not to feature at least one [[Like a Version]]. ==Top 20 Albums of 2010== Triple J Listeners voted for their favourite album of 2010 in a similar format to the Hottest 100. Voters were allowed to vote for any album released in 2010 and were limited to ten votes.
